fatigue.detail: Plain rolled bottom flange; welded attachments are checked separately in the detail register.

notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 2 simply supported 45-ft bays, W36X529 girders, one 40-ton cab crane, on column caps over new W14X159 crane columns beside the existing W14X233 building columns (pinned bases, anchor rods and spread footings, crane-level rod X-bracing between the crane columns), with the rail, the top-flange ties and the column ties to the building columns, bearings and end stops; the building columns are checked for the tie forces with their existing load effects and carry no runway vertical load. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves flange-tie-saddle-weld 1.11, flange-tie-flange 1.05 for the estimated tie demands; on a crane column the top flange is tied to the building column, a flexible restraint: the girder twists more at the supports, and a welded saddle on the tied flange is a Category D/E attachment in that flange lateral bending): the tie is paired flat bars, which bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): the column gusset slides 0.438 in each way along the runway on longer sleeves (column-end slide, fillers at the girder gusset; checks tie-slide-*). Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The tie's column gussets at the bearing stiffeners do not fit on the example W14X211 building column flange (15.8 in wide) with their fillets: the example building column is the lightest heavier W14 whose flange takes them, W14X233 (fictitious; the survey replaces it, and a narrower surveyed flange needs the gussets rearranged). No W and channel cap pair of the catalog meets the girder sizing targets (the closest, W24X370 + MC18X42.7: tips ratio 2.37, vertical deflection 0.90, lateral 1.05 of the limits, screening estimates): the compact rolled W catalog (12 to 40 in deep) is sized in its place. No rolled W meets every screening target; the lightest near them, W36X529 (screening tips 1.03, vertical deflection 0.35, lateral 0.96, rail-head 1.83), is confirmed by the calculation of this runway: every girder check passes (lateral 0.97, rail-head 0.83, combined 0.70, torsion-normal 0.65). The screening estimates run 1.5 to 2.2 times the calculation on these heavy sections with flexible ends; the calculation decides.

selections.designed: Paired flat bars on a bearing-stiffener gusset
selections.reason: A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves flange-tie-saddle-weld 1.11, flange-tie-flange 1.05 for the estimated tie demands; on a crane column the top flange is tied to the building column, a flexible restraint: the girder twists more at the supports, and a welded saddle on the tied flange is a Category D/E attachment in that flange lateral bending): the tie is paired flat bars, which bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): …

No W and channel cap pair of the catalog meets the girder sizing targets (the closest, W24X370 + MC18X42.7: tips ratio 2.37, vertical deflection 0.90, lateral 1.05 of the limits, screening estimates): the compact rolled W catalog (12 to 40 in deep) is sized in its place. No rolled W meets every screening target; the lightest near them, W36X529 (screening tips 1.03, vertical deflection 0.35, lateral 0.96, rail-head 1.83), is confirmed by the calculation of this runway: every girder check passes (lateral 0.97, rail-head 0.83, combined 0.70, torsion-normal 0.65). The screening estimates run 1.5 to 2.2 times the calculation on these heavy sections with flexible ends; the calculation decides.

Confirmed by the calculation, not by the screening: every girder check of W36X529 passes (lateral 0.97, rail-head 0.83, combined 0.70, torsion-normal 0.65). No compact W meets every sizing target; the closest: screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 1.03, vertical deflection 0.35, lateral 0.96 and rail-head movement with twist 1.83 of their limits; flanges at least 10.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios. The closest section is within the limits but not the sizing margins: the calculation decides.

New crane column for a 40-ton crane (W12X65 to 7.5 t, W14X90 to 15 t, W14X109 to 30 t, else W14X132), pinned base, braced at the cap across the runway by the column tie and along it by the crane-level bracing. The W14X132 crane column does not fit its column cap (validateColumnCap); the lightest heavier W14 that passes.

selections.designed: combined with the building column, 132 in square; 150 in at the braced columns
selections.reason: Isolated 12 ft square crane-column footings 38 in from the building column would be 64 in into its 5 ft footing (6 in clear required): each crane column and its building column stand on one combined footing replacing the existing one, 11 ft square (12.5 ft at the braced columns), the building column shored and re-set on new anchor rods; sized for the base reactions; the braced columns' footing apart from the others' (the rods' uplift and shear along the runway), sliding resisted by the base friction and the soil's lateral bearing on the footing and its shear key (IBC §1806.3.1).

Column tie 0.625 in × 10 in with 3 0.875 in A325 bolts on sleeves in 1.5 in × 2.125 in vertical slots: the lightest within the 0.9 sizing target for the estimated column-tie force 36.522 kip (the girder bottom-flange force through the cap, bounded by the girder tie force estimate 34.66 kip; the crane column's eccentric top reaction 0.129 kip; the brace force 0.01P_r 1.733 kip; the calculation takes the bottom-flange force from the girder model) and its fatigue range 23.409 kip at all cycles; slot travel 0.291 in each way (the larger column shortening plus the erection tolerance).

The building column face from the girder web (the crane-column centerline): at least the crane column's half depth plus the column tie's clear gap, moved out by the tie sizing (to at most 30 in) where the tie needs the flexible length; the crane column stands 22.5 in clear of the building column.

The tie's column gussets at the bearing stiffeners do not fit on the example W14X211 building column flange (15.8 in wide) with their fillets: the example building column is the lightest heavier W14 whose flange takes them, W14X233 (fictitious; the survey replaces it, and a narrower surveyed flange needs the gussets rearranged).

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.), supplier's joint bars (deferred submittal) installed slip-critical: Class A surfaces, bolts pretensioned, re-tightened at 30 and 90 days.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
